claims.claim: Epiphanius was bishop of Salamis (also called Constantia), the metropolis of Cyprus.
Epiphanius was born near Eleutheropolis in Palestine, between 310 and 320.
Epiphanius died in 403 at sea on his return journey from Constantinople to Cyprus.
Epiphanius was elected bishop of Salamis in 367 and held the post for nearly forty years until his death.
The work is titled 'Homilia in assumptionem Christi' (Homily on the Assumption of Christ) and is attributed to Epiphanius, bishop of Cyprus.
The homily survives in Migne's Patrologia Graeca, volume 43, columns 477-485.
The homily's incipit is 'Κόσμος σώματος ἡ ἐπιτεθεῖσα τῷ σώματι κεφαλή' (The head placed upon the body is the adornment of the body).
The homily treats the feast of Christ's ascension with flesh, celebrating the bodily assumption of Christ into heaven.
The homily addresses the defeat of the devil and the raising of human nature through Christ's ascension.

A related but shorter recension of this homily material appears as 'In Ascensionem sermo 2' in PG 52, 793, attributed to John Chrysostom, while the fuller version appears as 'In Assumptionem Christi hom. 4' in Epiphanius's corpus.
Epiphanius was known as a strong defender of orthodoxy and gained a reputation for learning and asceticism.
